summary.intent: Fix a failing CI/CD build for the cipher-box project by resolving package build order issues.
summary.outcome: Fixed the CI build by converting parallel `--filter` flags to sequential build steps, ensuring `@cipherbox/crypto` is built before `@cipherbox/core` which depends on its type declarations.

repo: The monorepo has a dependency chain: @cipherbox/crypto must be built before @cipherbox/core due to type declaration dependencies.
The CI test job already used sequential steps correctly, but the build job used parallel --filter flags which don't respect inter-package dependencies.
CodeRabbit path exclusions need explicit entries for non-standard directory names like `models/` and root-level generated files like `openapi.json` — `!**/generated/**` glob is insufficient.

code.finding: Build job used multiple --filter flags (parallel execution) instead of sequential steps; the test job was already structured correctly with separate steps as a reference.
Added three explicit path filters for generated files: packages/api-client/openapi.json, packages/api-client/src/generated/**, and packages/api-client/src/models/**.

workflow: In Turborepo/monorepo setups, multiple --filter flags on a single command run tasks in parallel and do not respect cross-package type dependencies at build time.
When debugging monorepo build failures involving missing type declarations, check whether the dependency package has been built first rather than assuming a type error in source code.

friction: The CodeRabbit glob pattern `!**/generated/**` silently failed to exclude `models/` directory and root-level generated files, requiring manual investigation and explicit path additions.
CI build failure required inspecting the GitHub Actions run URL to identify the root cause of missing type declarations.
open_items: Verify the sequential build fix resolves the CI failure once the pushed workflow runs.
Consider whether the `models/` directory naming convention should be standardized to `generated/` to align with existing glob exclusion patterns.
